name: The Samaritan village, and the sons of thunder
charge: Refusing to receive him because his face was toward Jerusalem; James and John asking for fire from heaven
summary: A village of Samaria would not take him in, and James and John asked leave to call down fire as Elias did. He rebuked them, not the village: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of; the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. They went to another village.
offense: They did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
judgment: He turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village. The village was spared a sentence, and the disciples were taught the difference between Elijah's day and theirs; one of those two sons of thunder later went down to Samaria with Peter to lay hands on believers there.

entries.commentary: He gave the twelve power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases, and sent them to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick. Take nothing for your journey. Where they are not received, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
Herod is perplexed, hearing that John was risen from the dead, or that Elias had appeared, and says, John have I beheaded: but who is this?
Five loaves and two fishes feed about five thousand men, sat down by fifties in a company, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up.

Whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God. The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day. That word stood alongside all the power they had just seen, and they still could not hold the two together.

If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. What is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away? Whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed.

As he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias, who spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem. Out of the cloud came a voice, This is my beloved Son: hear him. And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone.

A father brings his only child, whom the disciples could not deliver, and Christ answers, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? He rebukes the unclean spirit, heals the child, and delivers him again to his father, and they were all amazed at the mighty power of God.

Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men. The saying comes straight after a devil the disciples could not cast out. He had power to give power, and would still be delivered into the hands of men. They understood it not, and feared to ask him.
There arose a reasoning among them which of them should be greatest, and he set a child by him and said, He that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

John reports one casting out devils in his name whom they forbade, because he followed not with them. Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us. Men who are not speaking against Christ and are teaching the same identity of the people are not to be forbidden merely because they do not stand with us.

The Samaritan village would not receive him, and James and John ask to command fire to come down from heaven. Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.

Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God. This is not a bar on burying your own father. It is leaving the affairs of those who are not keeping the commandments to be handled by them, while the work goes on. No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High. -

Ahaziah falls down through a lattice in his upper chamber and is sick, and sends messengers to inquire of Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, whether he shall recover. He turns to an idol rather than to the Most High for his answer. The angel of the Lord sends Elijah the Tishbite to meet the messengers and ask whether it is because there is no God in Israel that they go to inquire of Beelzebub. The word of the Lord is that Ahaziah shall not come down from his bed but shall surely die. When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. -

The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does. A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight. The angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go down with the third captain and not to fear him. Elijah delivers to the king the same word, that because he sent to inquire of Beelzebub as though there were no God in Israel, he shall surely die.

Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, comes by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

Nicodemus takes it literally and asks whether a man can enter the second time into his mother's womb. Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? He was a chief teacher, and men depended on him for the understanding of the law. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?

As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up. The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten, and Israel that looked and lived. The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son. This follows straight on from the serpent, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. A man can be comfortable and even do well in the darkness he was raised in. Coming into the light requires change, and refusing that change is what condemns him. The Pharisees and the rulers were not condemned by Christ; they condemned themselves by not humbling down to repent. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.

John's disciples notice that all men are coming to Jesus, and John answers, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven. I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him. He must increase, but I must decrease.

He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true. Not to receive it is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.

Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death. This is Saul who becomes Paul, part of the same people persecuting the church, killing disciples and women, thinking he was doing it for the right reasons. That is why the scripture says judge no one before their time; a man as evil as Saul was doing back there became Paul the apostle. At that time there was a great persecution against the church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Notice that unlike the other epistles, the book of Acts never closes with Amen, showing there is a continuation: the apostles come back on the scene and redo the Acts all over again, so the things that happened back then are the things that happen today. There will be a great persecution today. This gospel is a witness against the whole world. When you pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done, you are saying the Most High's will overpowers America's will, Russia's, China's, every nation racing for world domination. To preach a black Christ in the streets is to speak against the system that was designed to keep our people debased, a Christ with many crowns upon his head who takes the crowns of all the nations. They are not going to let a people they despise rise up and preach a gospel that overthrows the world superpowers and do nothing; it is going to be a great persecution. Gird your mind, study, pray, and apply, because wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of our time.
Devout men carried Stephen to his burial and made great lamentation over him. A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report.

As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service. Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

The people with one accord gave heed to the things Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles he did. Unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many that were possessed, and many taken with palsies and that were lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city.

Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people. Christianity works the same way, a binding spell over our people that covers the eyes from seeing the truth. You can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and they walk away not believing, or say they do not want to hear the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man can read something in front of them and they see something else.

But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.

Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity. The gall of bitterness is resentment and bitterness of spirit. Simon became jealous because the signs the Most High worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight; he fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning. This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere, spoke more eloquently, and went to the scriptures better without the status.

Then Simon answered, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me. And when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

The angel of the Lord told Philip, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went, and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship. People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him. Notice the humility of the brother. Rather than making his own assumptions, he admitted he did not understand. Some brothers and sisters lack that humility, claiming, I always knew I was Israel, or, the Most High spoke to me while I was in my sins, rather than saying, This is the first time I heard this, teach me. You had to be taught this Bible to know this Bible; the Most High is not just going to hand it to you out of nowhere. Expressing that you do not know keeps you in a low state and away from the spirit of preeminence and vainglory.

The place of the scripture he read was Isaiah: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who shall declare his generation, for his life is taken from the earth. The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

As they went on their way they came to a certain water, and the eunuch said, See, here is water, what doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they went down both into the water, and Philip baptized him. This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
